clue.text: Badly put clue, say, for iron-bark

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters of put, clue and say are jumbled

explanation.surface: A complaint about a poorly worded crossword clue offered for the word iron-bark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges the ten letters of PUT CLUE SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron-bark is the common name of several hard-wooded Australian gum trees of this genus.

clue.text: Ideal place for a posh hat to be carried

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage
a topi is a sun helmet, a pith hat

explanation.surface: Somebody's dream spot where a smart hat can be carried about.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's imaginary perfect commonwealth gave its name to any ideal place.

clue.text: Inquire about rites arranged for a star

indicators.note: about means the word for inquire goes around the other piece

parts.note: to inquire is to ask

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of rites are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asking about religious ceremonies being organised for a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal and 'arranged' the anagram one; 'star' looks like a celebrity but is the printed symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed star symbol used to mark a footnote is called by this name.

clue.text: Yorkshire resort's leaders ousted by unknown hand

indicators.note: the leading letters of the resort are pushed out and replaced by the next piece

parts.note: Scarborough is a seaside resort on the Yorkshire coast
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire seaside town whose chiefs have been thrown out by a mysterious figure.
explanation.walkthrough: SC, the first two letters of SCARBOROUGH, give way to Y.
explanation.definitionFit: In whist and bridge this is a hand holding no card higher than a nine, named after an earl who bet against it.

clue.text: Effective way of counting votes

explanation.surface: A description of an impressive method of tallying ballots.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling blow is effective and striking; a teller counts votes, and the counting is this act.

clue.text: Distance between bridge supports is nine inches

explanation.surface: A statement that the gap between piers of a bridge is just nine inches.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch between two piers of a bridge has this name, as does the old hand-width measure of nine inches.

clue.text: After warning, move furtively to the outer border

indicators.note: after says the word for moving furtively comes behind the warning

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
to edge is to move slowly and stealthily

explanation.surface: Someone, having been warned, slinks off towards the perimeter.
explanation.definitionFit: In bookbinding this is the outer edge of the pages, opposite the spine.

clue.text: A man without funds runs to a moneylender

parts.note: a pawn is a chess man
broke means having no money
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A penniless man hurries off to borrow cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawnbroker lends money against goods left as security.

clue.text: Where some Asians worship a deity in Pennsylvania

indicators.note: in places a and the deity inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
a deity is a god

explanation.surface: Asian immigrants worshipping a god somewhere in the state of Pennsylvania.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiered tower is a Buddhist or Hindu temple building in East and South Asia.

clue.text: University sport confused a student about the position of the body

definitions.text: about the position of the body

indicators.note: confused means the letters of U and sport are muddled

parts.note: L, a learner, is a student

explanation.surface: A muddled college sport bewilders a student wondering how to hold the body.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a paraphrase: the adjective means concerning posture. 'confused' rearranges U plus SPORT as POSTUR.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective means relating to posture, the way the body is held.

clue.text: Cut short, this meal doesn't require much time

definitions.text: Cut short, this meal doesn't require much time

parts.words: Cut short, this meal doesn't require much time
parts.note: the formal name of a midday meal, shortened, gives its everyday name; a quick bite needs little time

explanation.surface: A remark that a hurried meal takes hardly any time.
explanation.walkthrough: Clipping the last three letters off the formal word gives the everyday word for the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the formal word for a midday meal, which shortened becomes the everyday word.

clue.text: Garment worn by Indians in Williams, Arizona

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words Williams Arizona

explanation.surface: Indians in the small town of Williams, Arizona, are wearing a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indians' points to Native Americans in Arizona, but the garment is South Asian; it straddles WilliamS ARIzona.
explanation.definitionFit: A long draped cloth wrapped as a dress, worn chiefly by women in India.

clue.text: In the main it's the culmination of a space mission

definitions.text: In the main it's the culmination of a space mission

parts.words: In the main it's the culmination of a space mission
parts.note: the main is the sea, and capsules used to end their flights by landing in the ocean

explanation.surface: Something mostly true about the end of a space mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads like 'mostly' but means at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Early crewed capsules ended their flights by parachuting down into the ocean.

clue.text: Campanologist pinching metal is the chief miscreant

indicators.note: pinching means holding the metal inside the word for the bell person

parts.note: a campanologist is a bell ringer
lead is a metal

explanation.surface: A bell ringer caught stealing metal is the main troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the person who leads others in wrongdoing or a riot.

clue.text: Blow also absorbed by abandoned woman

parts.note: abandoned means left

indicators.note: absorbed by means the word for also is soaked up inside the others

parts.note: her stands for a woman
and means also

explanation.surface: A jilted woman takes a blow on top of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A punch thrown with the weaker hand in boxing is called this.

clue.text: Sound philosopher determined to secure managerial action

indicators.note: sound signals that the philosopher's name is heard, not seen

parts.note: John Locke was an English philosopher
out, as in 'out to win', means determined to

explanation.surface: A sensible thinker resolves to bring about some management decision.
explanation.walkthrough: Locke sounds like LOCK; 'to secure' is a link with a nod to lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Employers shut workers out of their workplace in a dispute, the bosses' counterpart to a strike.

clue.text: Conspirator a Scotsman? That, adds spice!

parts.note: Cinna is one of the plotters against Caesar in Shakespeare
mon is the Scots form of man

explanation.surface: A plotter who is a Scot: that adds some flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried aromatic bark of a tropical tree is used as a spice.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory part of ship for use in slack periods

parts.note: off means substandard, as food that has gone off
the peak is the narrow part of a ship's hold at the bow or stern

explanation.surface: A poor section of a vessel to be used when things are quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: This describes times of lower demand, when fares or tariffs are cheaper.

clue.text: Salaried model making a recommendation

parts.note: a pro, a professional, is paid
a poser is one who poses, like an artist's model

explanation.surface: A paid fashion model offers some advice.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who puts forward a motion is the one offering a recommendation.

clue.text: Dark patch in which newspaper's going to ruin

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
pot, as in going to pot, means ruin

explanation.surface: A gloomy area in which a tabloid is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SUN is a British tabloid; 'going to' links to the idiom go to pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark spot on the sun's surface, cooler than its surroundings.

clue.text: Mavis's boy takes horse in great haste

annotationWithheld.why: Mavis's boy takes horse in great haste (4,6): SON (boy) and RUSH (great haste) are clear, but no reading of 'takes horse' gives the G, T and H between them without a word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Mavis's boy takes horse in great haste

clue.text: Honour given by a king to a poet

parts.note: OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour
R, rex, is a king

explanation.surface: A monarch bestows an award on a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omar Khayyam was the Persian poet of the Rubaiyat.

clue.text: Potential buyers accumulate about 500

indicators.note: about means the word for accumulate surrounds the number

parts.note: to amass is to accumulate
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Would-be customers piling up to around five hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the mass public targeted by advertising, seen as consumers.

clue.text: Game for military detachments, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for detachments is heard spoken

parts.note: drafts are detachments of soldiers

explanation.surface: A game for military detachments, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The board game known in America as checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the British name of the board game Americans call checkers.

clue.text: Outside Arkansas he makes a fast buck, perhaps

indicators.note: outside means the word he sits around the state abbreviation

parts.note: AR is the postal abbreviation for Arkansas

explanation.surface: A man in Arkansas makes some quick money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a fast buck' reads as easy money; a buck is a male hare, a fast animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is the male of this swift long-eared animal, so the clue gives an example.

clue.text: Unusually pleased to accept square as base

indicators.note: to accept means the jumbled word takes the next piece inside it
unusually means the letters of pleased take an odd order

parts.note: a T-square, so T

explanation.surface: Someone surprisingly happy to take a square as a foundation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' turns PLEASED into PEDESAL, and 'to accept' takes T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base on which a column or statue stands.

clue.text: Dog reproducing low sounds?

explanation.surface: A dog making deep noises.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog that barks is a playful word for it; also a loudspeaker designed for bass notes.

clue.text: Record rare purchase made by firm

parts.note: to enter is to record in a register
prise, leverage, is a rare spelling of purchase as grip

explanation.surface: A firm records an unusual acquisition.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a business or company.
